standard.title: Construct with media languages
standard.description: use media languages, media technologies and production processes to construct representations that communicate ideas, perspectives and/or meaning
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can use media languages and technologies to construct representations that communicate identifiable ideas or stories. They can apply basic shot types and make deliberate compositional decisions. They have not yet worked with the full production process — pre-production, production, post-production — or communicated perspectives and meaning through multi-element works.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students use media languages, media technologies and production processes to construct representations that communicate ideas, perspectives and/or meaning.

nodes.label: Media languages for perspective and meaning
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify how technical elements (shot type, angle, lighting, sound, text) communicate perspective and meaning — going beyond basic identification to explaining the communicative function.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify two technical elements (e.g. shot angle and lighting) in an existing work and explain how each communicates a perspective or creates meaning for an audience.
nodes.typical_width: Analyse how technical elements (shot types, angles, lighting, text in title sequences, Foley sounds) communicate perspective and meaning in existing works; use Viewpoints questions to frame analysis; connect technical choices to intended audience response.
wider: Analyse a short film sequence that communicates conflict through camera angles, lighting and/or costume without dialogue — identifying how each technical choice communicates a perspective and discussing what would change if the choices were different
Investigate how a soundscape uses volume, layering and voice to create a sense of environment — comparing two soundscapes for the same scene and explaining what meaning each creates
nodes.hinge_reason: Understanding how technical elements communicate perspective and meaning is the conceptual prerequisite for making deliberate production choices — without it, production decisions are aesthetic preferences rather than communicative strategies.

response_modes.reason: Use Viewpoints questions explicitly: 'What images will I use and in what order?', 'What does this camera angle communicate about this character's power?' Students need to practise the reasoning chain from choice to communicative effect.

success_criteria: Student can identify at least two technical elements in a media work
Student can explain how each element communicates a perspective or creates meaning for the audience

nodes.label: Production processes
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can plan and carry out a production using at least two stages of the production process (planning, capture, editing) — making deliberate decisions at each stage.
nodes.minimum_width: Use at least two production process stages (e.g. plan a shot list or storyboard, then capture footage; or capture footage and then edit/sequence) to produce a media element.
nodes.typical_width: Apply production process stages to construct a work — camera and framing decisions during capture, Foley sound creation, text application to images, editing and sequencing; use pre-production planning (storyboard, shot list) to guide production decisions.
wider: Create a soundscape using Foley sounds and recorded sounds (found objects, voice, recording technology) to accompany a moving image — applying production planning and experimenting with volume, layering and voice across multiple takes
Investigate and use digital or analog storyboarding as a pre-production tool — plan a short film, stop motion or comic strip, then rearrange the boards to change narrative meaning before producing

response_modes.reason: Production process fluency requires repeated practice — students who skip planning or who don't review and select media elements produce accidental rather than intentional representations. Invest in the full cycle, not just capture.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The range of production modalities at Y3-4 (photography with costume/setting, soundscape creation, moving image with Foley, collaborative publication) is genuinely diverse — students who work across multiple production types develop much stronger production instincts.
success_criteria: Student applies at least two stages of the production process when constructing a media work
Student makes and can explain at least one deliberate production decision at each stage

nodes.label: Representations communicate perspectives
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can construct a complete representation — using media languages and production processes to communicate ideas, perspectives and/or meaning for an audience.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce one media arts work using deliberately chosen media languages and at least one production process, and explain how the choices communicate a perspective or meaning to the intended audience.
nodes.typical_width: Produce representations across two or more forms or contexts (photo sequence communicating emotion, short film communicating conflict, soundscape communicating place, collaborative zine); connect technical choices to communicative intent; reflect on whether the representation communicates the intended meaning.
wider: Create a short film that communicates connection to a place in the community — drawing on First Nations Australian media arts works about Country/Place for inspiration, and using camera, lighting and sound to convey feeling without dialogue

Create a comic book, photo series or zine that communicates the maker's perspective on an idea significant in their lives — using layout, image selection, text and visual elements deliberately to create meaning for a specific audience

response_modes.reason: This node integrates technical language understanding with production process skills — the produced work is evidence that both are operating together. Ensure students can articulate the connection between their choices and their communicative intent.

success_criteria: Student produces a media arts work that communicates an identifiable idea, perspective or meaning
Student can explain at least two media language or production choices they made and how those choices serve the communicative intent
